2 . Facts of the case reveals that on 11.09.022 a missing report has been lodged by the father of victim at Police Station Gadwa District Singrauli, stating that on 06.09.2022, his brother's wife was unwell and was taken to Ghorawal Hospital for treatment.

At that time, his daughter, namely Vimla Devi Pal, aged about 19 years, along with other minor children of the NEUTRAL CITATION NO.

On 10.09.2022 at about 11:00 AM, his niece, Pannu Devi, informed him that Vimla Devi had gone somewhere else.
On his complaint, Police Station Gadwa District Singrauli has registered the missing report on 11.09.2022 as Missing Report No. 27/2022.

After the missing report, the victim was recovered from her village on 15.09.2022 and police has recorded her statement under Section 161 of Cr.P.C on 28.09.2022, wherein the respondent No. 2 victim specifically stated that she was with applicant from 11.09.2022 to 15.09.2022 and no wrongful act had been committed by the applicant, Vimlesh Pal and Anil Pal.
A copy of the statement under Section 161 of Cr.P.C. is the part of this petition.
Thereafter, her statement under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. was also recorded before the concerned Judicial Magistrate on 22.09.2022.

After the investigation, the SDOP Chitrangi, District Singrauli Bal Govind Pal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 4 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/119121570/

sentences.text:
Thereafter, victim has filed a private complaint under Section 156 (3)
along with Section 200 of Cr.P.C. wherein respondent No.2 victim, contrary to her earlier statements recorded before the concerned Court under Sections 161 of Cr.P.C. and Section 164 of Cr.P.C. as well as the contents of the missing report, alleged that on 20.01.2020, when she was about 17 years of age, the applicant committed rape upon her on the pretext of marriage and thereafter applicant had promised to marry her after she attained the age of 18 years.

She further alleged that on 11.09.2022, the applicant came to her house, again promised NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:9927 3 MCRC-28780-2024 to marry her, and took her to Singrauli, where he committed rape upon her without her consent.

She further alleged that when she opposed the act,
the applicant assured her that they would solemnize marriage in a temple; however, he neither married her nor fulfilled his promise.

Thereafter, the applicant allegedly left her in the village stating that he would not marry her and thereafter she made prayer for registration of FIR under Sections 376(3), 376, 420, 363, 366 of IPC and Section 5/6 of POCSO Act.

Again on the same point, the police has initiated the inquiry and submitted the report before the SDOP, Chitrangi, District Singrauli on 30.01.2023 and wherein it is found that applicant No. 2 under the pressure of her father and family members has submitted the false application.

After completing the investigation, the FIR has been registered against the present applicant on 12.09.2023 under Sections 376(2), 376, 420, 463, 366 of IPC and Section 5/6 of POCSO Act at Crime No. 304/2023 at Police Station Gadwa District Singrauli.
After completing the investigation, charge sheet has been filed before the concerned authority.

3 . Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the registration of the FIR and filing of the charge sheet are bad in law and accordingly the said FIR including the charge sheet and all subsequent proceedings, deserves to be quashed.
It is further submitted that on 11.09.2022, the missing report has been filed by the Rajnarayan Pal at Police Station Gadwa District Singrauli.
During the investigation of the missing report, the police has recovered the present victim.

Thereafter, police has recorded the statement under Section 161 of Cr.P.C. wherein respondent No. 2 has specifically stated that she was NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:9927 4 MCRC-28780-2024 with the applicant from 11.09.2022 to 15.09.2022 and no wrong things has been done by the applicant,
Vimlesh Pal and Anil Pal.

Thereafter police has recorded the statement under Section 164 of Cr.P.C.
before the concerned Magistrate.

Counsel for the petitioner further submitted that in order to falsely implicate the applicant and under pressure from family members, respondent No. 2 filed an application under Section 156(3) read with Section 200 of the Cr.P.C. after a delay of three months from the lodging of the missing report and after recording of her earlier statements under Sections 161 and 164 of the Cr.P.C.

In the said application, respondent No. 2, contrary to her earlier statements recorded under Sections 161 and 164 of the Cr.P.C. and the contents of the missing report, she made fresh allegations against the appellant.

4. Learned counsel for the applicant has relied the paras 21 and 24 of the judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Deepak Gulati Vs. State of Haryana, (2013) 7 SCC 675 , where it has been held as under:-

sentences.text: Hence, it is evident that there must be adequate evidence to show that at the relevant time, i.e. at initial stage itself, the accused had no intention whatsoever, of keeping his promise to marry the victim.

There may, of course, be circumstances,
when a person having the best of intentions is unable to marry the victim owing to various unavoidable circumstances.
The "failure to keep a promise made with respect to a future uncertain date, due to reasons that are not very clear from the evidence available, does not always amount to misconception of fact.
In order to come within the meaning of the term misconception of fact, the fact must have an immediate relevance."

Section 90 IPC cannot be called into aid in such a situation, to pardon the act of a girl in entirety, and fasten criminal liability on the other, unless the court is assured of the fact that from the very beginning, the accused had never really intended to marry her.

24. If the prosecutrix was in fact going to Ambala to marry the appellant, as stands fully established from the evidence on record, we fail to understand on what basis the allegation of "false NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:9927 5 MCRC-28780-2024 promise of marriage" has been raised by the prosecutrix.

We also fail to comprehend the circumstances in which a charge of deceit/rape can be leveled against the appellant,
in light of the afore-mentioned fact situation."

5. Learned counsel for the applicant has further relied the judgment o f Dhruvaram Murlidhar Sonar Vs. State of Maharashtra, (2019) 18 SCC 191 a n d Kunal Chatterjee Vs. The State of West Bengal and others, 2025 LiveLaw (SC) 765 in Special Leave Petition (Crl.) No. 7004/2025, w herein the Apex Court held that where a consensual relationship exists and the allegation is based on a promise of marriage, such facts must be carefully examined and do not automatically constitute rape,
particularly in the absence of supporting evidence.
6.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the respondent/State has opposed the prayer of applicant and submitted that there is no illegality in registration of the FIR.

It is further submitted that after the investigation,
Trial Court has already recorded the statement of complainant which shows that the trial has already commenced and that there is nothing on record to grant a clean chit to the applicant.
On the aforesaid pretext, he prays for dismissal of this petition.

7. In view of objection raised by the learned counsel for the State and the submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, this Court is required to determine whether the subsequent complaint filed by the same party, alleging the same offences against the same person, is maintainable or not.

After going through the record and looking to the case diary and considering the facts and circumstances of the case, the nature of the evidence relied upon by the prosecution particularly the inordinate delay in lodging the FIR clearly suggests that the present criminal proceedings NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:9927 6 MCRC-28780-2024 initiated against the applicant are nothing but an abuse of process of law.
The lower Court ought to have invoked its inherent jurisdiction in the case of the applicant as well, as it did while quashing the proceedings against the remaining accused.

9. Any pending interlocutory application, if any, stands disposed of accordingly.
